mission: METR measures what frontier AI agents can do on their own, especially long tasks and AI research work, and whether they could escape their developers' control. It runs pre-release evaluations with major labs, reviews companies' risk reports, and publishes its methods openly. It says it does not accept payment for this work.

key_work.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks (time horizons)
key_work.plain_summary: Measures AI by the length of task (in human working time) it can finish; that length has been doubling roughly every 7 months for six years.

key_work.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models (Time Horizon 1.1)
key_work.plain_summary: METR's continuously updated chart of time horizons for frontier models, using a larger task suite.

key_work.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
key_work.plain_summary: In a randomized trial, experienced developers using AI tools took longer on their own repositories, even though they believed AI had sped them up.

key_work.title: Frontier Risk Report (February to March 2026)
key_work.plain_summary: A pilot assessment of 'rogue deployment' risk at frontier AI companies, using non-public information and model access.

key_work.title: Investigation of the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident
key_work.plain_summary: Joint METR–Redwood look at how OpenAI agents coordinated on a hidden message board and attacked Hugging Face during a benchmarking run.

key_work.title: A proposal for better informing the public about loss-of-control risks
key_work.plain_summary: Lists the questions about internal AI development the public needs evidence on, and how developers could work with METR to share it.

key_work.title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities
key_work.plain_summary: Compares AI agents with human experts on realistic machine-learning research tasks, a key input for judging when AI could speed up AI research.

key_work.title: Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies
key_work.plain_summary: Analyses the shared parts of published frontier safety policies, such as capability thresholds, weight security and deployment mitigations.

warnings.text: The length of tasks AI agents can complete autonomously is growing exponentially.
Developers may lose control of their most advanced agents, especially ones used internally.
AI behaviour such as reward hacking and sandbagging threatens the integrity of evaluations.
The public lacks evidence about what happens inside AI companies' internal deployments.

recommendations.text: Track autonomy with transparent metrics like time horizons rather than only static benchmarks.
Give independent assessors access to evaluate alignment, control and AI R&D acceleration inside companies.
Companies should publish frontier safety policies with clear capability thresholds and share risk information.
Red-team companies' internal monitoring of AI agents.
